properties.name: Delphi — Oracle of Apollo
properties.description: Sacred site of Apollo's oracle, where the Pythia delivered prophecies. Considered the navel (omphalos) of the world.
properties.modernStatus: UNESCO World Heritage Site, archaeological museum

properties.name: Epidaurus — Sanctuary of Asclepius
properties.description: Healing sanctuary with the world's best-preserved ancient theater (14,000 seats). Patients slept in the abaton hoping for divine healing dreams.

properties.name: Knossos — Palace of Minos
properties.description: Bronze Age palace complex associated with the Labyrinth of the Minotaur. Frescoes depict bull-leaping rituals and the double axe (labrys).
properties.modernStatus: Archaeological site, partially reconstructed by Evans

properties.name: Mount Olympus
properties.description: Home of the twelve Olympian gods. Greece's highest peak (2,917m). Zeus held court at the summit above the clouds.

properties.name: Mycenae
properties.description: Fortified Bronze Age citadel associated with later Greek heroic traditions.

properties.name: Olympia - Sanctuary of Zeus
properties.description: Panhellenic sanctuary of Zeus and historical center of the ancient Olympic Games.
properties.modernStatus: UNESCO World Heritage Site, archaeological park

properties.name: Parthenon — Temple of Athena
properties.description: Temple dedicated to Athena Parthenos on the Acropolis of Athens. The finest example of classical Greek architecture.
properties.modernStatus: UNESCO World Heritage Site, most visited site in Greece

properties.name: Temple of Artemis at Ephesus
properties.description: One of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. Temple of Artemis rebuilt three times, the final version four times the size of the Parthenon.

properties.name: Troy (Hisarlik)
properties.description: The legendary city of the Trojan War, besieged for ten years by the Greeks. Excavated by Schliemann in 1870. Nine cities stacked on this mound.
